text: both have been studied in acute renal failure, and ularitide has also been studied in heart failure. Recombinant forms of atrial natriuretic peptide (carper- itide, p.1241) and brain natriuretic peptide (nesiritide, p.1347) are used in the management of acute heart failure. The currently available natriuretic peptides have short half-lives and have to be given parenterally. Other approaches to manipu- lating their effects have been investigated, including the use of atriopeptidase inhibitors (neutral endopeptidase inhibitors; neu- tral metalloendopeptidase inhibitors), such as candoxatrilat and ecadotril (sinorphan) to prolong the half-life of endogenous atrial natriuretic peptide. Compounds such as omapatrilat (p.1361) that inhibit both neutral endopeptidase and angiotensin-converting enzyme are also being studied. ◊ References. 1. Tan ACITL, et al.
